weather_notes: Farm newly acquired; trees not yet bearing.

First recorded harvest year. Source: Delta Packing Co. of Lodi 'Crop Insurance Worksheet Summary' + grower settlement statements (Lot 59) -- exact figures, not an estimate. Bing sold at $1.60/lb, Brook (Brooks) at $1.56/lb. Matches the crop-insurance production report's 30,514 total exactly. REAL CIMIS DATA CHECK (analysis/02_real_calibration_2024_2026.py, station 262 Linden): the chill/GDD model puts dormancy break at Feb 13 2024, not January -- and January 2024 had real hard freezes down to 25.5F (Jan 8) that would likely have damaged an active bloom. This suggests the reported 'January' bloom is an approximate memory and true bloom more likely started after mid-February (consistent with a good harvest, since Jan's freezes would predate bloom). No heat days >=95F and no single rain event over the 1.1in cracking threshold in the Apr-May pre-harvest window -- consistent with a normal, undamaged season.

Confirmed 0 yield. Cause reported as likely weather: untimely frost and/or untimely hot weather. REAL CIMIS DATA CHECK (analysis/02_real_calibration_2024_2026.py): chill requirement was met Jan 26 2026 -- earlier than 2024 -- so insufficient chill is not the driver. A real frost event Feb 20-21 2026 (29.2F) is the leading candidate IF bloom had already started by then (chill was satisfied 3+ weeks earlier, so this is plausible timing for early bloom). Separately, real heat >=95F shows up June 11-13 and mid-to-late July (up to 100.3F on Jul 14) -- but that's well after the farm's typical ~May harvest window seen in 2024, so it's a weaker fit unless 2026's season timing shifted substantially. STILL NEEDS INPUT: confirm which of these (the Feb frost, or something in the June-July heat) actually matches what was observed on the ground, and roughly when bloom/fruit-set happened this year.
